pages.title: Ruthcliffe Lodge - Bed and Breakfast in La Motte, Vermont
pages.description: The Ruthcliffe Lodge is a bed and breakfast on the shores of Lake Champlain on historic Isle La Motte, Vermont. Book a reservation today!
pages.text:
Ruthcliffe Lodge - Bed and Breakfast in La Motte, Vermont
Life is simple. Just add water .
BOOK YOUR VACATION TODAY
About Us
A secluded island paradise awaits. . .
Situated on the shores of Lake Champlain on historic Isle La Motte, this Vermont Bed and Breakfast - the Ruthcliffe Lodge - commands a panoramic view of the Green Mountains of Vermont. If you are traveling to Vermont, our secluded island paradise makes the perfect summer, overnight getaway or fall side trip. Only one hour from Montreal, Canada and Burlington, Vermont, it is also the ideal stopping place en route to these northern destinations.
Information
Enjoy Your Stay

Accommodations
Six lakeside guest rooms with unparalleled views of Lake Champlain; all uniquely decorated in themes characteristic of the region. Free Wi-Fi is also available.
Learn More

Activities & Nearby Attractions
Swimming, boating, canoeing, fishing, cycling, hiking, bird watching, and nearby golf. Take a stroll along the shores of the lake, or simply relax and take in the sun on our perfectly-positioned Adirondack chairs.
Visit a variety of nearby attractions:  local marble quarries, apple orchards, state parks, antiquing, crafts, and shopping, and so much more.
Discover More
Food & Drink
Please Accept our Apologies
Our restaurant is not currently open to the public. We are serving breakfast to our BNB guests only.
We do occasionally offer surprise, pop-up dinners.   To be included on our list, please leave us your contact phone number an we will get back to you.
Guest Food Service
A full breakfast is available for our overnight guests.  A list of area restaurants is available on our restaurant page .
Fine Wine & Full Bar Service
Our guests may enjoy a selection of imported and domestic wines in addition to full bar service during their stay.
Guest Reviews
Perfect Place
"We loved our stay at Ruthcliffe. It was peaceful, quiet and clean with a lovely spot on the lake. Breakfast was top notch. My wife said the waffles were by far the best she ever had in her life. I wish we had a chance to have a dinner there , we had read reviews from Frommers and other sources who said the food was incredible. Based on breakfast I would say it’s likely true. There is a campground near, but you don’t even notice it’s there.  We had lovely bike rides each morning on a quiet 10 mile loop where we saw lots of wildlife.  This in all aspects was a 10 for us.  If you're looking for peaceful, quiet and clean and a chance to relax and have stellar breakfasts and recharge your batteries, this is the perfect place!"
Richard R
Motorcyle Destination
"Took a nice motorcycle trip from NH to Ruthcliff. The Lodge is very cute and clean. Food there was outstanding. We were their last couple to stay there for the season. We even had breakfast with the incredible owners on the deck. Mary and Tim."
Gooddrummer
Something for Everyone
"Well located and plenty to do - I brought my paddleboard and my friend used a kayak from the property.  On another day, we biked to Saint Anne's Shrine.  We drove a quick hour or so south to the Shelburne Museum.  It has the best American folk art exhibits.  Something for everyone!"
Maria A.
Delightful, Relaxing Island Stay
"Delightful, relaxing island stay! Our stay at Ruthcliffe Lodge made our visit to Isle La Motte extra special. Clean, comfortable rooms feet away from the east shore of Lake Champlain. Delicious breakfast on the deck every morning and a wonderful dinner for extended family and friends. We booked 3 of the six rooms and couldn’t have been more comfortable or well cared for. We will certainly be back. ."
Merriew4

pages.text:
About Ruthcliffe Lodge - Located in La Motte, Vermont
About Ruthcliffe Lodge
Ruthcliffe Lodge Tradition
As second-generation husband and wife owners, we have kept up the Ruthcliffe tradition. Over the years, our rustic lodge has become renowned for its hospitality and fine foods. If you call for reservations, you'll likely get Kathy on the phone. And, it is Chef Mark who creates your fabulous meals. We invite you to come and experience Ruthcliffe for yourself!
Ruthcliffe is named after Mark's mother, Ruth, and the cliffs along the shoreline.  The lodge was originally built in 1951 by local craftsmen and family members. In 1957, we added a separate facility and opened to the public.
In 2001, we added a sitting room for reading, playing games, or just watching TV.
Today, Ruthcliffe Lodge contains 6 lakeside rooms, a restaurant and bar, and so much more.
Owners
Mark & Kathy Infante
Boston Globe ARTICLE
A Champlain Beauty - Vermont: Isle La Motte
By Judith Gaines, Globe Correspondent | April 18, 2004
The northernmost of the Champlain Islands, Isle La Motte also is the most remote, least commercialized, and most peaceful of the lot. Once you've crossed the old causeway that links it to the mainland, you enter a serene little world apart in an unusually picturesque and interesting farm burg.
About seven miles long and two miles wide, Isle La Motte looks something like a lozenge floating in the lake roughly 20 miles south of the Canadian border. Its population -- 300 or so year round -- is predominantly French Canadian, and the town layout reflects this. There's no town common, for instance, nor any white-spired church. The town center is a crossroads near which a country store with some gas pumps, a town hall, a post office, a firehouse, and a library all loosely clustered. Several of these buildings are made from elegant, locally quarried limestone.
The old schoolhouse houses the historical society and a museum. A quirky pink lighthouse stands on the island's northwest corner.
''It's feminine and sweet, just like me," quips Erika Bayer, who keeps the automated beacon.
What this town exudes is its own distinctive rural charm. Its only traffic light sits in Howard and Polly Schwenker's backyard, an inoperable totem their son gave them as a joke. ''It's the only traffic light within 26 miles," Howard Schwenker said with a chuckle.
Locals seem particularly proud of their pets, which come up frequently in conversations. The library features a large, framed photo of Keisha, an unusually sociable collie ''known for being good about visiting people in town," says trustee Joyce Tuck. The library also helps support itself with sales of a calendar featuring photos of a different local pet each month: dogs, cats, rabbits, horses, even a pet elk.
''It can be kind of quiet and isolated here, especially in winter," Tuck said. ''So you really get to know your animals, and your neighbor's animals."
A few locals rent out cabins or cottages, and there's a lakeside campground, but otherwise the main tourist accommodations are Ruthcliffe Lodge , a charming and secluded B&B with motel-like rooms and a restaurant on the lake, or Terry Lodge of Isle la Motte, a simple farmhouse where a set meal is served family-style in the evenings at the dining room table. We stayed at the Ruthcliffe and happily could have passed several days just lounging by the lake and enjoying the cooking of chef and co-owner Mark Infante. His wife, Kathy, was friendly and helpful, with lots of suggestions for things to see and do.
The island is flat, offering lovely views of Vermont's Green Mountains in one direction and New York's Adirondacks in another. Bicyclists seeking a mild and scenic excursion love the terrain and the lack of traffic. The island environment seems to moderate the climate somewhat, making it warmer than other communities this far north. Swimming, boating, and other water sports are popular here from about May to October, as is walking down the country lanes that crisscross the island. The Ruthcliffe rents bikes, canoes, and kayaks for $15 a day.
There's also an underlying reason -- literally -- to visit this place. The bedrock of the southern third of the island is one of the few visible remnants of the Chazy Reef, about 480 million years old, that once stretched 1,000 miles along what later became the North American continent. Scientists believe that in those days, the only living creatures inhabited the seas, and the reef grew over a period of about 10 million years as their calcium carbonate remains slowly accumulated, layer upon layer. Then the reef tilted.
''Now you can walk from south to north on the island, from the oldest to the youngest sections of the reef, and it's like a museum of this very primitive life on Earth," said Linda Fitch, who heads the Isle La Motte Preservation Trust. She gave a little tour, pointing to fossils of cabbage-like stromatoporoids and twiggy bryozoa in the 20-acre Fisk Quarry Preserve, and to assorted swirling gastropods and other exotic fossils just a mile or two away in the younger Godsell Ridge, where she hopes to preserve 81 additional acres.
Isle La Motte ''provides the most complete database in the world for this chapter of the Earth's history," Fitch said. ''It's a time capsule of ancient reef-building."
Much more recently, several significant events happened on the island. At a sandy beach on its western shore, the explorer Samuel de Champlain may have landed, when he discovered the lake and the region in 1609. Fifty-seven years later, a French captain named Pierre de La Motte -- for whom the island is named -- built a fort on the spot, dedicating it to St. Anne, mother of the Virgin Mary. The stockade was Vermont's first white settlement, and the state's first Roman Catholic Mass was celebrated here.

Lakeside Rooms
Ruthcliffe Lodge features six lakeside guest rooms with unparalleled views of Lake Champlain. Rooms are uniquely decorated in themes characteristic of the region. Each  room is comfortably furnished and features such charming details as hand-stenciled walls, handmade wall quilt, wicker chairs, and a Vermont-marble verandah overlooking the shores of the lake.
